input: In the context of an ongoing effort to improve performance on a moulding cell, it is worth noting that a defect-reduction project reportedly delivered a meaningful improvement over the course of one quarter, with the reject rate moving from 3.9% to 2.3%. When this improvement is considered against a production level of 94k units per year, the change is said to avoid about 1504 rejected units per year, which can be viewed as a substantial operational benefit. At the same time, however, it should also be kept in mind that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates have not been adjusted for that shutdown. In other words, the figures are presented on an as-run basis rather than on a normalised basis that attempts to remove the influence of the shutdown period. This is important because the annual avoided count is derived by applying the improvement to the stated yearly volume, rather than by drawing on a separate measurement from another period. Overall, the passage presents a lower reject rate and a corresponding reduction in rejected units, while also acknowledging, albeit in a somewhat qualified way, that the comparison period contained a planned shutdown and that no adjustment has been made for it in the reported rates.
target: A defect-reduction project on a moulding cell cut the reject rate from 3.9% to 2.3% over one quarter. At 94k units per year, the change avoids about 1504 rejected units per year. The annual avoided count uses the stated production volume as its basis; the count is not a separate measurement from another period. The quarter included a planned shutdown. Rates are not adjusted for the shutdown, so the reported change is the change in the recorded reject rate for the quarter as run. The result keeps two statements apart. The rate moved between the stated start and end values during the quarter, and the annual avoided count follows when the improvement is applied to the stated yearly volume. No adjustment removes the shutdown, estimates a shutdown-free rate, or restates the quarter on a different operating basis. That limit belongs with the headline figures because the shutdown formed part of the quarter in which the lower rate was recorded. A reject rate compares rejected units with production over the same period, and the two rates here are read on that common basis. The unadjusted form does not claim that operating conditions in the quarter matched any other quarter. The project result is a lower reject rate for the moulding cell and the corresponding avoided-reject count at the stated volume, with the shutdown left inside the comparison period and the basis stated beside the figures.
